en: 'Amr ibn Muhammad al-Naqid, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali, 'Ubaydullah ibn Sa'id, and Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umar al-Makki all narrated to us from Ibn 'Uyaynah—and the wording is Ibn Abi 'Umar's—Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, 'Amr ibn Dinar narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: I said to Ibn 'Abbas: "Nawf al-Bikali claims that Musa (peace be upon him), the companion of the Children of Israel, is not the Musa who was the companion of al-Khadir (peace be upon him)." He said: "The enemy of Allah has lied! I heard Ubayy ibn Ka'b saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) saying: 'Musa (peace be upon him) stood up to deliver a sermon among the Children of Israel, and he was asked: "Which of the people is most knowledgeable?" He said: "I am the most knowledgeable."' He said: 'So Allah reproached him because he did not refer knowledge back to Him, and Allah revealed to him: "Indeed, a servant among My servants at the junction of the two seas is more knowledgeable than you." Musa said: "O my Lord, how can I meet him?" So it was said to him: "Carry a fish in a basket, and wherever you lose the fish, he is right there." So he set out, and his young companion set out with him—he was Yusha' ibn Nun. Musa (peace be upon him) carried a fish in a basket, and he and his young companion set out walking until they reached the rock. Musa (peace be upon him) and his young companion slept, and the fish struggled in the basket until it slipped out of the basket and fell into the sea.' He said: 'And Allah held back the flow of water from it until it became like an archway. It was a passage for the fish, and it was an astonishment for Musa and his young companion. So they set out for the remainder of their day and their night, and Musa's companion forgot to inform him. When morning came, Musa (peace be upon him) said to his young companion: "Bring us our morning meal; we have certainly suffered fatigue from this journey of ours."' He said: 'And he did not suffer fatigue until he had passed beyond the place he had been commanded to reach. His young companion said: "Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? Indeed, I forgot the fish, and none made me forget to mention it except Satan, and it took its course into the sea amazingly." Musa said: "That is what we were seeking!" So they retraced their footprints, following their tracks.' He said: 'They retraced their tracks until they reached the rock, and behold, he saw a man covered with a cloth. Musa greeted him with salam, and al-Khadir said to him: "Where in your land is there any greeting of peace?" He said: "I am Musa." He asked: "Musa of the Children of Israel?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Indeed, you possess knowledge from the knowledge of Allah which Allah taught you and which I do not know, and I possess knowledge from the knowledge of Allah which He taught me and which you do not know." Musa (peace be upon him) said to him: "May I follow you so that you teach me of what you have been taught of sound judgment?" He said: "Indeed, you will never be able to have patience with me, and how can you have patience over that which you have not encompassed in knowledge?" Musa said: "You will find me, if Allah wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any matter." Al-Khadir said to him: "Then if you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I make mention of it to you." He said: "Yes." So al-Khadir and Musa set out, walking along the seashore. A ship passed by them, and they spoke to the crew asking them to carry them. They recognized al-Khadir, so they carried them both without fare. Then al-Khadir approached a plank from the planks of the ship and pulled it out. Musa said to him: "A people carried us without fare, yet you targeted their ship and damaged it to drown its people? You have certainly done a grave thing!" He said: "Did I not say that you would never be able to have patience with me?" Musa said: "Do not blame me for what I forgot, and do not make my affair difficult for me." Then they left the ship. While they were walking along the seashore, behold, a young boy was playing with some boys. Al-Khadir took hold of his head and severed it with his hand, killing him. Thereupon Musa said: "Have you killed a pure soul without retaliation for a soul? You have certainly done an evil thing!" He said: "Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me?" He said: And this was sterner than the first. Musa said: "If I ask you about anything after this, then do not keep company with me; you have received from me an excuse." So they set out until, when they came to the people of a town, they asked its people for food, but they refused to offer them hospitality. Then they found in it a wall about to collapse, so he restored it'—meaning it was leaning. 'Al-Khadir did with his hand like this, and restored it. Musa said to him: "A people whom we came to and they neither hosted us nor fed us; if you wished, you could have taken a payment for it." He said: "This is the parting between me and you. I will inform you of the interpretation of that over which you could not have patience."' The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: 'May Allah have mercy upon Musa! I would have loved for him to have had patience so that more of their story would be narrated to us.' He said: And the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: 'The first instance from Musa was due to forgetfulness.' He said: 'And a sparrow came and perched upon the edge of the ship, then dipped its beak into the sea. Al-Khadir said to him: "My knowledge and your knowledge have not diminished from the knowledge of Allah except like what this sparrow has diminished from the sea."' Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: And he used to recite: 'And there was before them a king who seized every sound ship by force.' And he used to recite: 'And as for the boy, he was a disbeliever.'"
